title: Book One · Chapter 153: Mum’s Own Card
story:
Mum wants to write her own display card. Ronan brings her the plain paper after supper. He has already left a space for her name.

She looks at the little lines he has drawn. “You think I write very small.”

“I can bring a larger sheet.”

“Please.”

He brings one. She puts the blue bag beside it and begins. The first line says: I made this bag for my things. The second explains the handles. The third tells about her test of the handles. She put weight inside, then changed the handles.

Ronan watches her write her name in Chinese at the bottom. He saw that name under his earlier picture. This time Mum writes the whole card herself.

“Can you write this: I made it for my family?” he asks.

“This one was for me.”

“But you help us.”

“I do. I also carry my own things.”

She opens the bag. There is a folded cloth and some thread wrapped in paper. Beside them is a book of simple patterns. Ronan has not seen the book before. “Is it new?” he asks.

“Borrowed,” she says. “I return it next week.”

She shows him a page with several pocket shapes. Some close with a button. Some fold over at the top. Ronan likes a long pocket shape. It looks like a house with no roof.

Mum likes a different one. She marks the page with a strip of paper and closes the book. She does not have time to make every idea before the school day. There are paid repairs promised for Thursday.

“I can tell people you are very busy,” Ronan says.

“Tell them about this bag. I can tell people about my own work times.”

She smiles as she speaks. Ronan looks at the card. He wants to write about all her help for him. But Mum wants visitors to understand her bag.

Mum gives him the paper. “Pretend I am a stranger. Read my card.”

He reads. He reads the line about Mum's own things. Then he reads about the new handles. Her name is there too. There is no line saying she is the best mother in the world. He feels proud of her work already.

Mum puts the first small sheet beside the larger one. Ronan offers to throw it away. She turns it over instead. The back is still clean and can hold a work note. He watches her keep it in her sewing book. Mum can still write on the small paper. Ronan leaves it with her work book. The larger card goes into its own dry cover.

At school Mei reads it too. “May people touch the handles?” she asks. Ronan writes the question down. He knows the answer for pictures. He does not know it for the bag.

Mum says yes that evening, with clean hands. She chooses three light books to put inside. No stones at school. The books will give it a little weight. But the bag must stay light enough for children to lift.

Ronan adds a small card: TRY THE HANDLES GENTLY. He shows it to her. She agrees, and he keeps it.

Then she picks up a man's shirt. It needs a new cuff. Ronan goes outside and reads on the repaired stool. They are doing different work under the same light. When Mum calls him to hold a folded edge, he marks his page and comes. She asks him to hold the folded cloth. She points to the edge. He holds it there. Mum can ask for help herself.

---

重点表达：patterns＝缝制图样；cuff＝袖口；gently＝轻轻地。

情节提示：thread＝线；pocket＝口袋；repairs＝缝补活（名词）。

理解：1. Mum 为什么没有在卡片上写“为了家人制作”？2. 参观者将怎样试用袋子？
